info.title: HealthTrack API
info.description:
REST API for **HealthTrack**, a remote monitoring system for home-based cardiac rehabilitation. Patients exercise at home
with a heart rate band, blood pressure cuff, and pulse oximeter; the API ingests their readings, evaluates them against each
patient's exercise prescription, raises and routes alerts, and serves trend, adherence, and risk data to the rehab team.

Base path `/api/v1`. All bodies are JSON (UTF-8) except login (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`) and report downloads.
Every identifier in the examples matches the synthetic sample data loaded by `04_sample_data.sql`, so each example call can be
run against a freshly built database.

## Quick start

```bash
# 1. log in as a clinician (sample data; staff accounts also send mfa_code)
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/v1/auth/token \
  -d grant_type=password -d username=marcus.lee@healthtrack.example \
  -d 'password=HealthTrack-Demo-2026!' -d mfa_code=492817
# -> {"access_token": "eyJ...", "token_type": "bearer", "expires_in": 900, "refresh_token": "rt_...", ...}

# 2. open the worklist
curl -s http://localhost:8000/api/v1/worklist -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

# 3. patient app uploads a reading (as the patient)
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/v1/patients/00000000-0000-4000-b000-000000000005/vitals \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PATIENT_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: hb-5-202610211548" \
  -d '{"recorded_at":"2026-10-21T09:48:00-06:00","context":"exercise","heart_rate":138,
       "device_id":"00000000-0000-4000-c000-000000000051","source":"device"}'

# 4. acknowledge the resulting alert
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/v1/alerts/00000000-0000-4000-f000-000000000001/acknowledge \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"note":"Calling patient now."}'
```

## Authentication

| Item | Design |
|---|---|
| Login | OAuth2 password grant at `POST /auth/token`. Staff accounts require a 6-digit TOTP `mfa_code`. |
| Access token | Signed JWT, **15-minute** lifetime. Claims: `sub` (user id), `role`, `sid` (session id), `iss`, `aud`, `iat`, `exp`, `jti`. RS256 with rotating keys (`kid`) in production; HS256 with a secret from the environment is acceptable for local development. |
| Refresh token | Opaque 256-bit random value, **12 hours** for staff and **7 days** for patients. Stored only as a SHA-256 hash in `auth_sessions`. Rotated on every use; replaying an old refresh token revokes the whole session. |
| Passwords | bcrypt (cost 12) or Argon2id. At least 12 characters, checked against a breached-password list. Changing a password revokes all other sessions. |
| Lockout | 5 failed logins lock the account for 15 minutes (`users.failed_login_attempts`, `locked_until`). Error messages never reveal whether an email exists. |
| WebSocket | Browsers cannot send an Authorization header on a WebSocket, so `POST /auth/ws-ticket` issues a single-use, 30-second ticket for `GET /ws/stream?ticket=`. |

## Authorization: roles plus care-team scope

Access is decided by **role** (from the token) and **relationship** (is the caller on this patient's current care team, or is
this the patient's own record). Both checks run in the API dependency layer, and the database enforces the same relationship
rule again with row-level security (see below), so a bug in one layer does not expose data.

| Resource | patient | clinician | physician | admin | it_admin |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Own profile, password | RW | RW | RW | RW | RW |
| User accounts | | | | R (staff) | RW |
| Patient demographics | R own (edit contact) | RW care team | RW care team | RW all, no clinical data | |
| Care team assignments | R own | R care team | RW care team | RW | |
| Prescriptions | R own | R care team | RW care team (signs) | | |
| Vitals, sessions, activity, symptoms | RW own | RW care team | RW care team | | |
| Appointments | R own | RW care team | RW care team | RW | |
| Alerts (view, acknowledge, resolve) | | RW care team | RW care team | | |
| Alert rules, thresholds, escalation | | R | RW | R rules, RW escalation | |
| Risk scores, recommendations, reports | | R care team, review | R care team, review | | |
| Program metrics (aggregate) | | | R | R | |
| Audit log | | | | R | R |
| Device inventory | | assign | assign | | RW unassigned |

Blank cells return **403**. A request for a specific patient outside the caller's scope returns **404**, not 403, so the API
never confirms that a record exists.

## Security considerations

- **Transport:** TLS 1.2 or higher only, HSTS, no plain HTTP. CORS restricted to the dashboard origin.
- **Defense in depth:** for every request the API opens a transaction and runs `SET LOCAL app.user_id`, `app.user_role`, and
  `app.request_id` from the verified token. PostgreSQL row-level security policies (`can_access_patient`) then filter every
  patient-scoped table, and the API connects as `healthtrack_api`, a role that does not own the tables and cannot bypass them.
- **Least privilege and minimum necessary:** administrators see demographics and aggregate metrics but no clinical readings;
  IT administrators manage accounts and device inventory and see no PHI. Patients reach only their own record.
- **Input validation:** request schemas set `additionalProperties: false` and mirror the database CHECK constraints
  (ranges, formats, cross-field rules), returning **422** with field-level errors. The database rejects anything that slips past.
- **PHI out of URLs and logs:** identifiers are random UUIDs; name search uses `POST /patients/search` so names never appear in
  query strings or access logs. SMS notifications carry only severity and a link.
- **Audit:** every PHI read and write is recorded (who, what record, when, outcome, request id). Database triggers capture
  writes automatically by column name without copying PHI values; the API logs reads. The audit log is append-only.
- **Abuse limits:** login 5 per minute per IP and account; general API 120 requests per minute per user; ingestion 600 readings
  per minute per patient. Limits return **429** with `Retry-After`. Page size is capped at 200 to slow bulk extraction, and report
  exports are audited as `export`.
- **Idempotency:** POSTs that create readings or sessions accept an `Idempotency-Key` header, and each reading may carry its own
  `idempotency_key`, so retries after a dropped connection never create duplicates.
- **Clinical safety:** implausible readings are stored but flagged `suspect` and never alert; critical alerts are never suppressed
  and escalate after 15 minutes without acknowledgment; system-generated recommendations require clinician approval.

## Conventions

- **Time:** ISO 8601 with offset (`2026-10-21T09:48:00-06:00`); stored as UTC. Day-level summaries use the patient's time zone.
- **Pagination:** `page` (from 1) and `page_size` (1 to 200, default 50). List responses return `{items, meta}`.
- **Errors:** RFC 9457 problem details (`application/problem+json`) with `request_id` and, for 422, an `errors` array.
- **Status codes:** 200 OK, 201 Created (with `Location`), 204 No Content, 400 malformed, 401 unauthenticated,
  403 role not allowed, 404 not found or out of scope, 409 state conflict (double booking, duplicate open alert,
  already resolved), 422 validation, 423 account locked, 429 rate limited.
- **Correlation:** send `X-Request-ID` (UUID) or the server generates one; it is echoed in every response and audit entry.
- **Versioning:** the major version is in the path (`/api/v1`). Additive changes do not bump it.

## Sample accounts (synthetic data only)

All sample accounts use the mock password `HealthTrack-Demo-2026!`.

| jordan.pike@healthtrack.example | it_admin | Accounts and device inventory |
